newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Family of murdered Australian still back beheading.
newsitem.headline: Family of murdered Australian still back beheading.

text.p: The brother of an Australian nurse murdered in Saudi Arabia said his family still believed the maximum penalty -- death by beheading -- was appropriate for her two accused colleagues if they were convicted.

However, Frank Gilford said his family was prepared to consider any other options which may be raised by the presiding Saudi judges or the lawyers defending British nurses Deborah Parry, 41, and Lucille McLaughlan, 31.

"We still feel the maximum penalty is appropriate for the crime at this stage," Gilford told Reuters by telephone from his home in the small south Australian town of Jamestown, 200 kilometres north of Adelaide.
"We can look at other options but it will not necessarily mean to say we will take them. That is as far as we can go now."

Gilford's sister, Yvonne, 51, was found murdered in her dormitory room at the King Fahd medical complex in the eastern oil city of Dharhan on December 11 last year, having been stabbed, bludgeoned with a hammer and suffocated.
Her two British colleagues, who have retracted earlier confessions to the crime and deny being responsible, now face beheading if they are convicted.
Under Saudi law, the victim's family could spare their lives and accept financial compensation known as blood money.
The women's defence lawyers said the court hearing had been adjourned for three weeks to give the Gilford family time to consider a settlement which could spare the lives of the accused.
